C0007.summary: In order for a private, nonprofit entity to be considered to be an eligible entity for purposes of section 9902(1) of title 42, the entity shall administer the community services block grant program through a tripartite board described in paragraph (2) of 42 U.S.C. 9910(a) that fully participates in the development, planning, implementation, and evaluation of the program to serve low-income communities.
C0007.scope_text: In order for a private, nonprofit entity to be considered to be an eligible entity for purposes of section 9902(1) of this title

C0008.summary: The members of the board referred to in paragraph (1) of 42 U.S.C. 9910(a) shall be selected by the entity and the board shall be composed so as to assure that: (A) ⅓ of the members of the board are elected public officials, holding office on the date of selection, or their representatives, except that if the number of such elected officials reasonably available and willing to serve on the board is less than ⅓ of the membership of the board, membership on the board of appointive public officials or their representatives may be counted in meeting such ⅓ requirement; (B)(i) not fewer than ⅓ of the members are persons chosen in accordance with democratic selection procedures adequate to assure that these members are representative of low-income individuals and families in the neighborhood served; and (ii) each representative of low-income individuals and families selected to represent a specific neighborhood within a community under clause (i) resides in the neighborhood represented by the member; and (C) the remainder of the members are officials or members of business, industry, labor, religious, law enforcement, education, or other major groups and interests in the community served.

C0009.summary: In order for a public organization to be considered to be an eligible entity for purposes of section 9902(1) of title 42, the entity shall administer the community services block grant program through: (1) a tripartite board, which shall have members selected by the organization and shall be composed so as to assure that not fewer than ⅓ of the members are persons chosen in accordance with democratic selection procedures adequate to assure that these members (A) are representative of low-income individuals and families in the neighborhood served; (B) reside in the neighborhood served; and (C) are able to participate actively in the development, planning, implementation, and evaluation of programs funded under this chapter; or (2) another mechanism specified by the State to assure decisionmaking and participation by low-income individuals in the development, planning, implementation, and evaluation of programs funded under this chapter.
C0009.scope_text: In order for a public organization to be considered to be an eligible entity for purposes of section 9902(1) of this title
C0009.choice_text: Administer through either (1) a tripartite board meeting specified democratic selection, representation, residency, and active participation requirements, or (2) another State-specified mechanism assuring decisionmaking and participation by low-income individuals.

inventory.U0000: In order for a private, nonprofit entity to be considered an eligible entity for purposes of section 9902(1) of this title, the entity must administer the community services block grant program through a tripartite board that is described in paragraph (2) and that fully participates in the development, planning, implementation, and evaluation of the program to serve low-income communities.
inventory.U0001: The members of the tripartite board of the private nonprofit entity must be selected by the entity.
inventory.U0002: The tripartite board of the private nonprofit entity must be composed so as to assure that one-third of the members of the board are elected public officials holding office on the date of selection, or their representatives.
inventory.U0003: For the tripartite board of a private nonprofit entity, if the number of elected officials holding office on the date of selection who are reasonably available and willing to serve on the board is less than one-third of the board's membership, membership of appointive public officials or their representatives may be counted toward meeting the one-third requirement.
inventory.U0004: The tripartite board of the private nonprofit entity must be composed so as to assure that not fewer than one-third of the members are persons chosen in accordance with democratic selection procedures adequate to assure that these members are representative of low-income individuals and families in the neighborhood served.
inventory.U0005: Each representative of low-income individuals and families selected under clause (i) to represent a specific neighborhood within a community on the private nonprofit entity's tripartite board must reside in the neighborhood represented by that member.
inventory.U0006: The tripartite board of the private nonprofit entity must be composed so as to assure that the remainder of the members are officials or members of business, industry, labor, religious, law enforcement, education, or other major groups and interests in the community served.
inventory.U0007: In order for a public organization to be considered an eligible entity for purposes of section 9902(1) of this title, the entity must administer the community services block grant program through either a tripartite board satisfying the requirements of paragraph (1) or another mechanism specified by the State under paragraph (2).
inventory.U0008: Under the tripartite board alternative for a public organization, the board members must be selected by the organization and the board must be composed so as to assure that not fewer than one-third of the members are persons chosen in accordance with democratic selection procedures adequate to assure that they are representative of low-income individuals and families in the neighborhood served, reside in the neighborhood served, and are able to participate actively in the development, planning, implementation, and evaluation of programs funded under this chapter.
inventory.U0009: Under the alternative mechanism for a public organization, the program must be administered through another mechanism specified by the State to assure decisionmaking and participation by low-income individuals in the development, planning, implementation, and evaluation of programs funded under this chapter.

claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0007 accurately represents the condition and requirement of 42 U.S.C. 9910(a)(1) governing private nonprofit entities seeking eligible entity status under section 9902(1), correctly retaining the governing condition, the mandatory administration through a tripartite board, and its full participation duties.

Claim C0008 faithfully captures the detailed selection, tripartite composition ratios (1/3 public officials, not fewer than 1/3 low-income representatives, remainder community interests), the appointive official exception, and the residency requirement. However, it completely omits the governing prerequisite lead-in from subsection (a)(1) ('In order for a private, nonprofit entity to be considered to be an eligible entity for purposes of section 9902(1) of this title'), converting a conditional qualification into an overbroad unconditional mandate.

Claim C0009 fully and accurately captures the requirements for public organizations under 42 U.S.C. 9910(b), including the governing condition to qualify as an eligible entity under section 9902(1) and the disjunctive choice between a tripartite board meeting low-income representation and participation standards or an alternative State-specified mechanism.

unit_judgments.rationale: The requirement that a private nonprofit entity administer the CSBG program through a tripartite board that fully participates in development, planning, implementation, and evaluation to be considered an eligible entity is fully covered by C0007.

C0008 states that board members shall be selected by the entity, but omits the governing prerequisite lead-in from subsection (a)(1) governing private nonprofit entities seeking eligible entity status under section 9902(1).
C0008 captures the one-third elected public official composition requirement, but lacks the governing scope qualification from subsection (a)(1).

C0008 correctly retains the exception permitting appointive public officials when fewer than one-third elected officials are reasonably available and willing, but the linked claim omits the governing scope lead-in.

C0008 includes the requirement that not fewer than one-third of the members be democratically chosen representatives of low-income individuals and families, but fails to include the governing scope prerequisite.
C0008 retains the requirement that representatives of low-income individuals and families reside in the neighborhood represented, but inherits the overbroad scope error of the claim.

C0008 includes the requirement that the remainder of the board be officials or members of business, industry, labor, religious, law enforcement, education, or other major community groups, but lacks the governing scope condition.
C0009 fully covers the condition that a public organization administer the program through either a tripartite board or another State-specified mechanism to be considered an eligible entity.
C0009 completely incorporates the public organization tripartite board alternative, including democratic selection, low-income representation, residency, and active participation requirements.
C0009 fully retains the alternative permitting administration through another State-specified mechanism assuring decisionmaking and participation by low-income individuals.
